tabs.title: Company Overview
tabs.content:
**Marrolyn Retail** runs a global e-commerce storefront with customers in North America, Europe, and Asia. Seasonal sales events cause traffic to spike to more than 20 times the normal baseline for short periods.

**Current Environment:**
- The storefront web application is hosted on backend pools of VMs in three Azure regions.
- A single public entry point must accelerate and secure traffic before it reaches any regional backend.
- The security team has flagged repeated OWASP Top 10 style attack attempts (SQL injection, cross-site scripting) against the storefront in the past quarter.

tabs.title: Web Platform Requirements
tabs.content:
**Global delivery:**
- Traffic must be routed to the closest healthy regional backend and static assets should be cached at edge locations close to shoppers.
- One of the regional origins is intentionally kept off the public internet entirely — Marrolyn requires a fully private path from the global entry point to that origin.
- Microsoft-managed WAF rule sets and bot protection are both mandatory requirements for the global entry point.

**Backend health:**
- Each regional backend pool must be monitored so unhealthy VMs are automatically removed from rotation.
- The team wants to probe a custom `/health` path rather than rely on the default probe behavior, and wants to fail a server out after 2 consecutive bad responses.

**Security rollout:**
- Because the storefront is business-critical, any new WAF policy must first run in a mode that logs matched rules without blocking legitimate shoppers, before it is switched to actively block attacks.
